submission.justification:
Crystal-K2 at 4 cm thickness is the optimal configuration for this low-background gamma spectrometer, achieving the best possible energy resolution (4.575% FWHM at 662 keV) among candidates that meet the stringent background requirements.

PERFORMANCE ACHIEVEMENTS:
- Energy resolution: 4.575% FWHM at 662 keV (best among viable options)
- Background rate: 0.3 counts/kg/day (well within 0.5 budget with 0.2 margin)
- Optimal thickness: 4 cm identified through comprehensive simulation (2-10 cm range)

CANDIDATE COMPARISON:
- Crystal-K1: Despite superior nominal resolution (2.9%), excluded due to excessive internal contamination (2.0 counts/kg/day) that exceeds the background budget by 4×, making it unsuitable for low-background screening operations
- Crystal-K2: Best balance of energy resolution and low-background compliance
- Crystal-K3: While offering excellent background performance (0.1 counts/kg/day), delivers 46.6% worse energy resolution (8.558% at optimal 6 cm thickness)

THICKNESS OPTIMIZATION:
Comprehensive simulations across five thickness values (2, 4, 6, 8, 10 cm) revealed clear optimal performance at 4 cm for Crystal-K2. Thicker configurations showed significant degradation (5.264% at 8 cm, 6.354% at 10 cm), likely due to increased light collection losses.

This configuration enables the facility to achieve its primary goal of best possible energy resolution for the assay programme while maintaining the essential low-background operation required for dark-matter experiment material screening.
